To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
latent infection can be induced in mice by low‐dose intratracheal infection with virulent mycobacterium tuberculosis, and that it is maintained by a type1 cytokine profile and the production of TNFα.
the intratracheally‐injected mycobacteria are able to establish latent or progressive infection in mice depending upon the dose used.

(1) we have established an animal model of latent tuberculosis; (2) latent tuberculosis is characterized by low and steady bacillary loads, without death of animals; (3) latent tuberculosis is associated with a Th1 cytokine pattern; (4) latent tuberculosis is also associated with a high level of TNFα expression; (5) latent tuberculosis is induced by low numbers of mycobacteria, and is maintained by a type‐1 cytokine pattern and by TNFα.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that control the outcome of mycobacterial infection in the lung.
the establishment and analysis of a model of latent tuberculosis in mice, and the results are discussed with respect to their relevance to the pathogenesis of the disease in humans.
the study of the mechanisms that lead to the persistence of latent infection in the lungs.

latent infection occurs in a variety of cells in histologically‐ normal lung, but that this phenomenon is not restricted to this tissue.
the experimental model of latent tuberculosis described in this paper is a useful tool for studying the immunological and pathophysiological events involved in the development of latent tuberculosis.
latent infection is characterized by low bacillary loads, granuloma formation and the expression of type 1 cytokines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
latent infection occurs in the presence of an active immune response, but in the absence of an overt histological response.
we established an experimental model for latent tuberculosis in mice, which allows the detailed immunological and histological study of the mechanisms of persistence and latency in vivo.
latent infection is characterized by a low and stable bacillar load, with a Th1 cytokine response, and a high bacillar load with a Th1/Th 2 cytokine pattern, and a high and unstable bacillar load.
The main takeaway from our work is that
latent TB is not the same thing as active TB and that it is not a benign infection.
latent tuberculosis is a disease that should not be underestimated.
